blocks.text:
## Tour highlights

In Rio, you can see the city from Sugar Loaf and Corcovado, walk along its famous beaches and experience how closely the ocean, mountains and city meet.

At Iguazu, you will see the falls from both sides. The Brazilian side offers a panorama of the cascades, while paths and walkways on the Argentine side take you close to the water, including the famous Devil’s Throat.

The Amazon brings a different experience: piranha fishing, jungle walks, a Caboclo village, boat trips and the meeting of the Rio Negro and Solimões. The two rivers flow side by side for several kilometres without mixing because their water differs in temperature and density.

After the sightseeing part of the trip, you have two free days in Búzios to swim, sunbathe, go snorkelling or windsurfing, or simply relax by the ocean.
